name: Lycopene
lead: Lycopene is the red carotenoid pigment that gives tomatoes, watermelon and pink grapefruit their colour. It is consumed through food, especially cooked tomato products, and as a supplement.

In skincare it is promoted as an internal photoprotective antioxidant. Intervention trials suggest small reductions in UV-induced redness and some markers of photodamage, but the effects are modest and lycopene does not replace sunscreen.

paras: Lycopene is a highly lipophilic molecule that accumulates in skin and is an efficient quencher of singlet oxygen and other reactive oxygen species. By limiting UV-driven oxidative damage and downstream inflammatory and matrix-degrading signals, it is thought to blunt part of the sunburn response. Absorption improves when it is eaten with fat and after heat processing.

Dietary and supplement doses are generally well tolerated. Very high intake can cause lycopenemia, a harmless orange tint to the skin that resolves after reducing intake. Many trials are small and often use tomato paste or industry-supplied extracts, so findings should be read cautiously.
